department: Department of Physics and Astronomy (School of Physical and Chemical Sciences)

deadline.value: Studentship deadline Jan 28 (the School's page gives no year; 2027 inferred from the 2026 cycle, when Science and Engineering studentships closed Jan 28, 2026). This applies to Queen Mary PGR studentships, STFC studentships and China Scholarship Council applicants. There is no fixed closing date otherwise, and self-funded students are accepted at any point in the year.
deadline.quote: STFC studentships can now be awarded to students from any country who satisfy the eligibility criteria. | Deadline - 28th of January | Queen Mary offers a number of university-funded studentships each year across a full range of academic disciplines. These include the waiver of tuition fees and tax-free maintenance costs. Deadline - 28th of January.

also.quote: Science and Engineering Studentships: Wednesday 28th January 2026
There is no fixed closing date for applications but you should remember that decisions on applications will be made as quickly as possible.
We will accept self-funded students at any point in the year.

supervisor.value: You must identify a potential supervisor and contact them first, usually by email. Only once they agree to consider your application do you apply formally, naming the supervisor on the form. This applies to self-funded applicants too.
supervisor.quote: Before applying, you will need to identify a potential supervisor for your PhD. | Once you have contacted a potential supervisor, and they have agreed to consider your application further, you will be required to make a formal application.

also.quote: Self-funding applicants should follow the guidelines outlined in our usual application process to identify a potential supervisor and secure their agreement to consider your application further before formally applying online.

funding.value: A limited number of funded projects (usually covering tuition fees plus a maintenance stipend) are advertised. Some funding is limited to UK residents. STFC studentships are open to any nationality but cover international tuition only in part.
funding.quote: We have a limited number of funded projects available which are advertised on our PhD project pages.

also.quote: Some of the funding available is limited to UK residents. | A full studentship lasting 3.5 years will cover the payment of tuition fees (in full for UK-based students, or in part for international students)

entry_route.value: Generally a first or upper-second-class (2:1) honours degree in a relevant subject (or a recognised overseas equivalent). A master's is desirable but not always essential, and projects may list specific requirements.
entry_route.quote: A first or upper second-class honours degree in a relevant subject area. | A masters qualification is desirable but not always essential. | Specific entry requirements or experience required will be listed on the relevant project page where applicable.

ielts_min.value: The physics department states IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, with 6.0 in writing and 5.5 in reading, speaking and listening.
ielts_min.quote: Academic IELTS: 6.5 overall, with a minimum of 6.0 in writing and a minimum of 5.5 in reading, speaking and listening

notes: The university's research Deadlines page still shows the 2026-entry cycle. The Physics research-degree page quotes IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 in writing and 5.5 in the other skills, while the School and university Band 4 pages say 6.0 in every skill. Applicants needing a visa may need an ATAS certificate before a CAS is issued. The Astronomy Unit has its own record (qmul--astronomy).
